summary: Third independent G3 English review of EFMP-302 Unit 5, against the frozen bundle at commit 0cb98a9 and the manifest at specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-05/G3-run003b/manifest.json (137 inputs, verified byte-for-byte with inputManifest(): zero missing, zero extra, zero digest mismatches, zero dirty inputs; skill_digest matched). Disposition: REVISE. Five of the nine unresolved run-002 findings are now verified closed, one is superseded by owner ruling D-2026-0001, and one (the rubric-table scroll region) is moot because the rendered geometry changed. Two blocking defects remain, both actionable with precise repairs and neither requiring an owner decision, which is why this run returns revise rather than the escalate of run 002. (1) The approved MCQ blueprint is still violated: topic 5.3 carries one MCQ of ten where content-spec.md requires at least two per topic, and sub-topic U5-10 carries none. Option order and markdown indentation were repaired; no item's topic assignment changed. (2) The occupational-status comparison in topic-02 remains an unsupported factual generalisation, rendered to the learner as a comparative table in fig-U5-4 and assessed by MCQ 7 and RRQ 6, while carrying none of the disclosure the unit applies to its other unsourced claims. One new uncertain finding concerns the hennessy2022 declaration, which under the amended rubric is judged on honesty and completeness rather than on retrieval: it records the retrieval failure but not the level of support, and is in tension with content-spec.md's own record of what was read, while topic-03 attributes three findings-level claims to the source with the word 'establish'. All six mandatory deterministic checks passed at exit 0 and real browser inspection was performed at 1280x900, 360x780 and A4 print media across all seven rendered pages.

BLOCKING, finding 'run002-f9-status-comparison'. docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-05/topic-02.mdx lines 118-122 asserts, of Pakistan specifically, that teaching 'typically has lower pay, a less selective entry route and less day-to-day autonomy' than medicine or law and 'greater security, substantial social respect in some communities' than many other occupations. specs/content/efmp-302/coverage/unit-05.md line 23 grounds U5-08 in demirkasimoglu2010 alone. The omission is determinate rather than ambiguous, because the unit applies the disclosure elsewhere and claims to apply it everywhere: topic-01.mdx lines 152-154 ('This unit cites no research for those practices, because none was verified while it was written ... offered as reasoned practice ... not as findings'), topic-01.mdx lines 79-81 and 90-94 (maslach2016 and skaalvik2020 scope), topic-01.mdx lines 178-180 (naparan2021 scope), index.mdx lines 32-39 ('Where no research supports a claim about Pakistani conditions, the unit says that too'), and specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-05.md lines 15-19 ('the scope of each is recorded below and restated in the prose wherever the source is used'). Repair: either source the comparison, or add at topic-02.mdx lines 118-122 the same one-sentence disclosure used at topic-01.mdx lines 152-154, and mark fig-U5-4 accordingly.

UNCERTAIN, finding 'new-hennessy2022-declaration'. Judged under the amended rubric on declaration honesty and completeness, not on retrieval. specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-05.md line 41 declares hennessy2022 under '## Unverifiable sources' with the attempt (ScienceDirect HTTP 403 to this host; EdTech Hub companion record 'serves metadata only'), the date ('Could not be retrieved on 2026-09-19') and the authorisation ('Owner ruling 2026-09-19 (D-2026-0001)'). It does not state the level of support, which is the one thing little2001's row at line 40 does state ('rests on title and bibliographic level only'). topic-03.mdx lines 49-58 then writes 'What it does establish is that teacher development opportunities in such countries are limited and often not informed by research evidence, that technology offers real potential to extend both formal programmes and informal peer learning, and that outcomes so far are mixed' - three findings-level claims from a source declared unretrievable, with no bound excerpt in specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/ (13 excerpts present; hennessy2022 and little2001 absent).

The tension is internal to the bound bundle: content-spec.md line 93 records 'Abstract read 2026-09-15' for hennessy2022 and summarises it as 'what technology does and does not deliver for teacher development in low- and middle-income countries', which would support the three claims at abstract level, while the unit's own declaration says metadata only. A reviewer cannot determine from the declaration whether 'What it does establish' is within what was actually read. Repair: state the support level in the '## Unverifiable sources' entry as little2001's entry does, reconciling it with content-spec.md line 93. Recorded as uncertain rather than blocking because the likeliest reading is an incomplete declaration of an abstract-level basis, not an overstated claim; it is not resolved on the evidence bound to this attempt.

Sentence and paragraph length are consistently within intermediate reach; the abstract material is always anchored to a concrete Pakistani instance before it is generalised - Miss Shahnaz's Tuesday (topic-01.mdx lines 26-38), Mr Rafiq's four demands (topic-02.mdx 26-35), Ms Sundas's forty tablets (topic-03.mdx 26-34), Mr Bilal and Miss Ayesha (topic-04.mdx 26-38).

The nine-part cycle is complete and genuine in all four topic files, not merely headed: situation, explanation, activity, check-your-understanding, summary, self-assessment checklist, practicum transfer task, summative task with a mini-rubric, further reading. Progression from classroom situation to explanation is real in each - e.g. topic-04.mdx opens on two teachers leaving the same meeting (26-38) and the explanation at 60-64 returns to Mr Bilal by name to diagnose him.

Misconceptions are named and attacked rather than listed: 'burnout is just being very tired' (topic-01.mdx 67-68 and 96-100), 'the home language is the problem' (topic-01.mdx 145-154), 'integrating technology means using it in every lesson' (topic-03.mdx 79-82), 'a teacher's status is fixed' (topic-02.mdx 135-145), 'the answer to difficult conditions is resilience' (topic-04.mdx 73-78). All five match the content-spec 'Common misconceptions' list, and the teacher notes give each a handling strategy (unit-teacher-notes.mdx 45-65).

Activities are feasible in the stated Pakistani/Sindhi context, with group size, materials and timing: topic-02.mdx 147-159 (groups of four, 30 minutes, no materials beyond the case), topic-03.mdx 101-111 (pairs, four supplied cases), topic-04.mdx 122-137 (ten minutes individual then pairs, 30 minutes, a single challenge-attack question). None requires equipment a government school lacks. The teacher notes anticipate the two places the context bites - unit-teacher-notes.mdx 92-99 gives a fallback when parent access is hard and when a practicum school has no technology at all, and 89-90 protects the host teacher from being audited.

Conceptual depth rather than word count: the want-versus-measure distinction (topic-02.mdx 78-97), the demands-and-resources mechanism that yields two levers rather than one (topic-01.mdx 100-108 and topic-04.mdx 84-88), and the three-region analysis whose payoff is the discrimination between an accurate judgement and an excuse (topic-04.mdx 60-64) are each carried through to an activity and an assessment item.

The unit refuses the two easy moves a unit on hard conditions invites: topic-01.mdx 128-131 declines to claim a resourceful teacher can substitute for missing resources, and topic-04.mdx 66-71 refuses to let the control distinction become an argument for quiet endurance. unit-teacher-notes.mdx 20-36 makes both an explicit teaching instruction.

NEW this run, minor, and not specific to this unit. At 360px every figure carrier is its own horizontal scroll container: <figure class="figure figure--diagram"> computes overflow-x auto with clientWidth 328 against scrollWidth 880 to 1030. The full figure is therefore reachable by touch and pointer and the document never scrolls horizontally, which is why the accessibility criterion passes. The container carries no tabindex, no role="region" and no aria-label, so a keyboard-only user at that width has no reliable way to pan the figure and a screen-reader user reaching it gets no announcement of what they have landed in. Mitigated in practice because each figure's alt text and each SVG's <title>/<desc> carry the instructional meaning in full. Worth addressing in the shared Figure component rather than in this unit.
